what_its_for: Pegvaliase-pqpz is used to lower high levels of phenylalanine (Phe) in the blood in adults who have phenylketonuria (PKU). PKU is a rare condition where your body cannot properly break down an amino acid called phenylalanine, which can build up to harmful levels. This medicine helps break down phenylalanine so your body can get rid of it.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) under your skin (subcutaneous injection). Your healthcare provider will teach you or a caregiver how to give the injection at home. Common injection sites include your stomach area (abdomen), thighs, or upper arms. Rotate the injection site each time to avoid skin irritation. Do not inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or scarred. The injection is usually given once a day, but your doctor may adjust how often you take it. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over many months. This is done to help your body get used to the medicine and to reduce side effects. A typical starting dose is 2.5 mg injected once a week for 4 weeks, then increased gradually. The maximum dose is 60 mg once a day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on how well your phenylalanine levels respond to treatment. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: Store pegvaliase-pqpz in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store the medicine at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 30 days, but once removed from the refrigerator it must be used within that time. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used needles and syringes in an approved sharps container right away.
what_to_avoid: Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy, faint, or have a severe allergic reaction after your injection. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause your phenylalanine levels to rise again. Avoid skipping doses because consistent use is important for this medicine to work properly. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, supplements, and herbal products you take before starting this medication, as interactions are possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help RIGHT AWAY if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) such as: difficulty breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe dizziness, fast heartbeat, or a drop in blood pressure. This medicine has a serious risk of anaphylaxis and must only be given in a setting where your doctor can monitor you, especially at the beginning. Also call your doctor if you notice: joint pain or swelling, rash, hives, or skin reactions at the injection site, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain that is severe, signs of depression or mood changes, or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Pegvaliase-pqpz works slowly over time. It may take several months to more than a year before you see a significant drop in your phenylalanine levels. The dose is gradually increased to get the best results while managing side effects. Your doctor will regularly check your phenylalanine blood levels to see how well the treatment is working. Be patient and do not stop treatment early — many patients see continued improvement with longer use.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may affect your baby and the risks and benefits need to be carefully discussed with your doctor. Women with PKU should work with their healthcare team closely during pregnancy to manage phenylalanine levels safely. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in people under 16 years of age. Older adults: There is limited information on the use of this medicine in adults over 65. Talk to your doctor about any special considerations for your age and health condition.
